Found it. In the pasted content modal (`UploadedFile.svelte` line 98), the close button has `hover:text-gray-800`. The modal background in dark mode is `dark:bg-gray-800` (from `Modal.svelte` line 100). So on hover, the icon color (`gray-800` = `#1f2937`) matches the dark background exactly — it vanishes.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- Tailwind's `hover:text-{color}` utilities have no automatic dark-mode counterpart — you must pair them explicitly with `dark:hover:text-{color}`.
- The modal's `dark:bg-gray-800` background is `#1f2937`, which is the exact same value as `gray-800` text, creating a zero-contrast situation only on hover.
- The default (non-hover) state uses `text-gray-500`, which has enough contrast on both light and dark backgrounds, so the issue only manifests on hover.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

The fix is a one-line addition of `dark:hover:text-gray-200` to maintain contrast in dark mode:

content.text:
`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- This is a classic dark-mode hover bug: the element is visible at rest and visible in light mode on hover, but the hover state was never tested against the dark background.
- Tailwind's responsive and state variant ordering matters: `dark:hover:text-gray-200` compiles to `.dark .dark\:hover\:text-gray-200:hover { color: ... }`, which correctly scopes the override to both dark-mode and hover simultaneously.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

The fix adds `dark:hover:text-gray-200` to the modal close button in `UploadedFile.svelte:98`. In dark mode the modal background is `gray-800` (`#1f2937`), so the old `hover:text-gray-800` rendered the icon invisible — same color as the background. The new dark-mode hover color (`gray-200` = `#e5e7eb`) restores full contrast.
